comments.text: Muinul Islam Because that simply isn't feasible. The project type in CSE499 is not predefined. It varies from faculty to faculty, and also students also have their own tastes. Some faculty might want AI projects, some might want IoT projects, some might want blockchain-based projects, and the list can go on, and students have similar criteria. So, how many such courses do you want to tag as prerequisites? Well, a lot! NSU doesn't even offer all the prerequisite courses of CSE499. Students can take different combinations of trail courses according to their preferences. Let's say I have a passion for AI, so I'll take CSE445/465/495/440. You might be passionate about networking and take networking courses as your trail. Someone might take software trail courses. If NSU imposes a condition that you can do CSE499 only if you are done with your trail courses, you'll never be able to graduate within 4-5 years. The reason is simple - your core courses, along with other courses like maths, physics, chemistry, biology, and GEDs, will take over three years to complete. Now, if you want to satisfy your prerequisites and then jump into CSE499, I'm sorry to say you will struggle to finish graduation within five years. Another thing to note is that, let's say you have finished your trail in AI, but you want to do your 499 project in blockchain. This prerequisite system, if enforced, will destroy any such chance of shifting. Last but not least, the trail courses are not enough. They serve as an introduction, and they are not designed in such a way that would make you an expert in your field. So, either way, you have to study on your own, and since you are a student of CSE, this is the least a faculty can expect from you. I hope I made it clear.
